summary: George Chemparathy is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1961–1964) and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as a professor at Utrecht University (~1973–1993).

George Christopher Molesworth Birdwood worked in Indology and archaeology. An Edinburgh M.D. graduate (~1849–1854), he was a professor at Grant Medical College (~1858–1868), curated the Government Museum, Chennai, founded the Victoria and Albert Museum, and served at the India Office (1878–1899).

George Cowgill was an archaeologist who studied at Stanford (~1948–1952) and Harvard (~1954–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2007).

George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London (~1861–1863). He held a post at University College London from ~1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès worked in archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at EPHE and Berlin under Alfred Foucher and others, he directed the EFEO (1929–1947), worked at the National Library of Thailand, and later taught at INALCO and the Sorbonne.

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Northwestern University (~1968–1972) and studied at the University of Sri Lanka. He served as Professor of Religion at Northwestern University (~1974–2012).

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago (1902) and Harvard (1903–1905). He held appointments at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).
George Ernest Ward was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at The Queen's College, Oxford, and Wadham College, Oxford (~1856–1860).

George Eugene Dunkel is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Hoffmann and earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1970–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Princeton, and the University of Zurich (appointed 1986).

George Everest studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1804–1806). He served as an assistant with the Great Trigonometrical Survey (1817) and later as Surveyor General of the Survey of India (1830–1843).

George F. Dales worked in archaeology and Indology, earning his Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania (~1954–1960). He held posts at the Royal Ontario Museum, University of Toronto, University of Pennsylvania, and the University of California, Berkeley (appointed 1972).
George Fletcher MacMunn was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (1888). He later served as Warden of Sackville College from 1939 to 1952.

George Foot Moore was a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale and Union Theological Seminary. He served as a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and at Harvard University (1902–1928), alongside a guest professorship in Berlin (1909–1910).

George Frederick Nicholl, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1877–1878). He served as Lecturer in Oriental Languages at Oxford (1878–1909) and Professor of Sanskrit and Persian at King's College London (1879).
George Gordon Rogers was an Indologist and linguist who completed studies at Bedford College and at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst (~1912–1914).

George Henry Rouse was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Regent's Park College (~1856–1860) and the University of London (~1858–1861), and later taught at Haverfordwest Baptist College (1867–1872).

George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who studied at Phillips Academy (~1858–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He subsequently held a long-standing academic post at Harvard University from ~1870 to 1913.
George Herbert Westcott was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Peterhouse, Cambridge (1882–1885). He held a post as a Fellow at the University of Allahabad in 1894.

George L. Hart is an Indologist and linguist who earned his Sanskrit PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1975) and served at the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–2013).

George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at MIT and Indiana University Bloomington under Roman Jakobson. He taught linguistics at Harvard (1965–1969) and served as a linguistics professor at the University of California, Berkeley (1972–2016).
